historicalContracts.name: OpFoundationUpgradeSafe
historicalContracts.note: While in Base's perimeter it was foundationSafe of the DeputyPauseModule (can swap the pause deputy, giving a unilateral path to pause Base withdrawals via the shared SuperchainConfig), co-owner (2-of-2) of the SuperchainProxyAdminOwner that upgrades that SuperchainConfig, and LivenessModule fallback owner of the Security Council.

historicalContracts.name: SuperchainConfig
historicalContracts.note: Shared Superchain pause switch used by Base while present: the guardian could pause Base withdrawals, blacklist dispute games, and switch the respected game type - direct freezing of project funds (opstack/SuperchainConfig template is critical today).

historicalContracts.name: OpFoundationOperationsSafe
historicalContracts.note: In the L2OutputOracle era it was OP_SIGNER of Challenger1of2 and could unilaterally delete Base's output roots (indefinitely freezing withdrawals); later a 2-of-2 co-owner of the Base Governance Multisig that owns Base's L1 ProxyAdmin (upgrade of the whole system).

historicalContracts.name: DelayedWETH_PermissionedGames
historicalContracts.note: Held the bonded ETH backing permissioned dispute games; compromise or malicious upgrade redistributes bonds and breaks the incentive layer of the proof system securing withdrawals (opstack/DelayedWETH template is critical today).

historicalContracts.name: DelayedWETH_PermissionlessGames
historicalContracts.note: Held the bonded ETH backing permissionless fault dispute games; compromise or malicious upgrade redistributes bonds and breaks the incentive layer of the proof system securing withdrawals (opstack/DelayedWETH template is critical today).

historicalContracts.name: L2OutputOracle
historicalContracts.note: Pre-fault-proof state root oracle: a fraudulent output root accepted here (via PROPOSER compromise or malicious upgrade) enables theft of all escrowed funds through OptimismPortal withdrawals after the 7d finalization window (opstack/L2OutputOracle template is critical today).
